gpu_policy.decided: owner, 2026-11-23, before any H GPU work
gpu_policy.reason: cuda5's GPU is shared with another user's training job (yields to other GPU users after ~100 s, restarts ~2 min after they leave) and a batch script of ~1 min GPU jobs (does not yield). In Measurement G, one clear sample followed by our ~35 s CPU start-up let the job return (overlap at 18:09).
gpu_policy.holder: code/gpu_holder.cu, one CUDA context of ours for the whole session; 'work' mode (one 1-block ~1 ms kernel every 100 ms) except while one of our GPU processes runs
gpu_policy.idle_check: 5 consecutive samples 2 s apart with no compute process other than the holder and none of our GPU jobs; otherwise retry every 300 s for up to 12 hours, then stop and report. The holder stays in 'work' through the check.
gpu_policy.per_process: the holder stays in 'work' through the process's CPU start-up (index load) and switches to 'idle' (no GPU work) as soon as a GPU context of ours other than the holder appears, before the warm-up rounds; back to 'work' when the process ends; times in logs/holder-switch.tsv. A process whose context is never seen stops the session.
gpu_policy.overlap: unchanged: 0.5 s poll + pmon during each process; a process that overlaps another user's GPU process is preserved as <tag>-overlap-<n> and rerun, at most 3 replacements per slot (experiments/2026-11-22-range-v3-tune/code/overlap.py; it classifies the holder as ours)
gpu_policy.effects: the holder cannot change our answers (every process is checked against the oracle) and issues no GPU work during the timed rounds; it holds ~150-250 MB; per-process peak memory excludes it; timing is validated against Measurement F's W=4096 cells (cross-session check)
gpu_policy.code: code/session_lib_h.sh (redefines wait_idle and run_slot; the tune session_lib.sh monitors are reused read-only)

inputs: code/build_indexes_h.sh: W=256 (PR #27 pin 0ad6531c..., content 90b86a65..., header positions/256), W=1024 (c7669620...), W=4096 (06368cee...) verified by SHA-256; W=512/2048 built from the pinned GSP (e838dfbf...) with build time, size, SHA-256 and round-trip check; queries data/derived/calibration-500.tsv; oracle: pinned top-1000 (302b63d4...), top-10/100/316 as its prefixes (top-10/100 equal to the pinned files byte for byte)
pre_registration_session: code/run_h_pre.sh: one-query probe per W at its largest k; gates for every (W, k) cell incl. k=316 (500 queries, 1 warm-up + 1 measured round, exact); feasibility table and GPU-time estimate (analysis/feasibility_h.py). Nothing timed.

part_2.registered: 2026-11-23, before any H timing (owner instruction; the launch is automated on cuda5 so it does not depend on the laptop)
part_2.grid: W in {256, 512, 1024, 2048, 4096} x k in {10, 100, 1000} (15 cells). Cells whose gate fails are infeasible; if any cell fails, the timing session is not started and the owner is asked.
part_2.k316: k=316 is added at every W only if the pre-registration estimate including it (analysis/feasibility.json estimate_minutes.grid_with_k316) is <= 90 minutes
part_2.gpu_time_rule: if the 15-cell estimate (estimate_minutes.grid) is > 90 minutes, the timing session is not started and the owner is asked
part_2.design: one cuda5 session (code/run_h.sh); 3 processes per cell, each 500 calibration queries x (3 warm-up + 20 measured rounds), batch 1, 256 threads, radix at every k (crossover 1); W rotated within each k: process round p runs the W list (256, 512, 1024, 2048, 4096) cyclically shifted by p; every timed output checked against the oracle prefix (exact, else the session stops)
part_2.statistic: per cell: pooled median, p95, p99 over the 3 x 500 per-process query medians of query_wall_ms; W / 4096 at the same k: geometric mean of paired (process round p, query) ratios, crossed bootstrap over processes and queries, 10,000 draws, seed 20261125 (analysis/analyze_h.py)
part_2.H1: best W per k: the W with the lowest geometric-mean ratio; it differs from 4096 only if its upper 95% bound is < 1
part_2.H2: best single W: regret(W, k) = ratio(W, k) / best ratio at k; choose the W with the smallest maximum regret across the timed k values, over the W timed at every k; ties (equal to 3 decimals) broken by the geometric mean of its ratios across k; the regret table is reported
part_2.H3: if H2's W is not 4096, report its gain per k and recommend it only if no k has an upper bound > 1.02
part_2.H4: at k=10, W=256 / W for every other W (paired, same session, 95% intervals); 'W=256 is best at k=10' only if every upper bound is < 1
part_2.upper_edge: W=4096 is the largest W tested; if it is best at some k, a larger W was not ruled out
part_2.diagnostic_profile: after timing, not timed: clock build (-DRBP_STAGE_CLOCKS), first 25 calibration queries, k=10 at W=256, 1024 and 4096, 3 + 5 rounds; setup, decode+add, local top-k, candidate write (mean per block, critical path), merge tail, kernel span; waves from the feasibility table
part_2.cross_session_check: W=4096 pooled medians against Measurement F's 0.403 / 0.455 / 0.833 ms at k = 10 / 100 / 1000 (descriptive)
part_2.gpu_policy: as part 1 (holder, 5-sample clear window, retry every 300 s for up to 12 hours from the timing launch, then stop and report)
